articles.title: Power Is No Longer an Input in Data Centers. It Is the Product.
articles.narrative: This article argues that power availability has become the primary determinant of value and site selection for data center development, rather than a mere input. The author contends that traditional real estate factors like land and fiber are secondary to the ability to deliver electricity when customers need it, especially for AI companies with rapid deployment timelines. This shift is forcing developers to engage more deeply with energy infrastructure, seeking out substations, transmission access, and gas connections, and re-evaluating sites based on existing electrical capacity and phased energization potential. The article concludes that 'digital dirt'—land with inherited, difficult-to-replicate infrastructure—is gaining new relevance, exemplified by former industrial sites like Paducah, Kentucky, which offer significant power and water infrastructure for AI data centers.

articles.title: Anthony Cohen of Northmarq: 5 Questions
articles.narrative: This article features an interview with Anthony Cohen, a managing director at Northmarq and co-leader of the firm's national net-lease and sale-leaseback group. Cohen discusses his career trajectory, starting from J.P. Morgan and moving into distressed debt brokerage before specializing in sale-leaseback transactions. He highlights the current market trend of high demand for accelerated depreciated assets like gas stations, car washes, and oil change sites, which offer significant tax benefits to buyers. Cohen also details a recent sale-leaseback transaction for a food manufacturer in Pennsylvania, where the strategic use of real estate generated substantial capital for facility upgrades.

articles.title: Sunday Summary: Sharp Left
articles.narrative: This article provides a summary of various commercial real estate news items, focusing on potential legislative impacts in New York, emerging financing options for affordable housing, and significant transactions across different asset classes. The upcoming New York State elections are highlighted as a potential catalyst for changes in retail rent control, rent-stabilized apartment regulations, and data center development moratoriums, though they may also foster affordable housing initiatives. The piece also covers the growing use of tax-exempt CMBS debt for affordable housing and the implications of the new 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act. Additionally, it details several major leases in New York City's retail and office sectors, a large student housing portfolio acquisition, and significant development and financing activities in South Florida and Washington, D.C.

articles.title: 'We Aren't Competitive': Power, Taxes Keep Colorado On The Data Center Sidelines
articles.narrative: Colorado is largely missing out on the artificial intelligence data center boom, a situation attributed by industry leaders to the state's tax structure and power supply challenges. Despite being home to several major data center companies, Colorado's high energy costs and unfavorable tax policies make it less competitive compared to other states that offer more incentives and cheaper power for these energy-intensive facilities. This has led to a significant portion of new data center development bypassing the state, impacting its potential for economic growth in the tech sector.

articles.title: £1B Property Group To Buy Huge Chunk Of Collapsed NCP Car Park Empire
articles.narrative: Martin Property Group is set to acquire 100 car park leases from NCP, a move that comes as driving habits are reportedly declining. This significant acquisition by the £1 billion property group reflects a strategic play in the evolving real estate landscape, potentially signaling a shift in asset class investment priorities.
